*   Question: "What causes the seasons on Earth?"
    *   Constraint: "One paragraph."

    *   The primary cause is the tilt of Earth's axis (approximately 23.5 degrees).
    *   As Earth orbits the Sun, this tilt causes different parts of the planet to receive varying amounts of direct sunlight at different times of the year.
    *   When a hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it experiences summer (more direct sunlight and longer days).
    *   When a hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun, it experiences winter (less direct sunlight and shorter days).
    *   Spring and autumn occur during the transitional periods when neither hemisphere is tilted significantly toward or away from the Sun.

The seasons on Earth are caused by the 23.5-degree tilt of the planet's axis as it orbits the Sun. Because of this tilt, different parts of the Earth receive varying amounts of direct sunlight at different times of the year. When a hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it experiences summer because the sunlight hits the surface more directly and the days are longer. Conversely, when a hemisphere is tilted away from the Sun, it experiences winter due to the more slanted angle of the sunlight and shorter daylight hours. The transitional seasons of spring and autumn occur when neither hemisphere is tilted significantly toward or away from the Sun.
